title: Feeling sure of the order
hook: You studied three words in order and feel sure of it. How sure should you be?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that feeling sure is not evidence, and only checking an attempt against the answer shows how much of it is right

misconception: If an answer feels familiar and you feel sure, it is probably right.
objective: Compare felt familiarity with a scored local reconstruction.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: You studied three words in order and feel sure of it. How sure should you be? Your attempt feels familiar. Before checking it, how many places do you know are right? Options: All 3 of 3: you feel sure / Unknown until checked / At least 2 of 3. Correct option: Unknown until checked. All fixture words are stipulated exercise data.

claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Held. "One attempt does not predict later recall" is an empirical claim marked convention, and no openable source supports it (Roediger & Karpicke 2006 is not openable here and is about retention, not prediction). It overstates the verified c2 boundary. Suggested fix (cm-lifehacks): "One check cannot tell you how well you will remember it later, but it does show which step to fix." | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED (was held in W-740; text unchanged). The first sentence is right for the stipulated scenario (steps 1, 2 and 4 match, so step 3 is the one to fix). The second, 'One attempt does not predict later recall', is a general empirical negative, labelled convention, with no source. It is broader than the lesson's own principle ('this single attempt cannot estimate future retention'), and as a general statement it runs against the usual finding that items recalled on a first test are more likely to be recalled later. I could not open a source to cite for that, so the dispute rests on the claim having no support and overreaching its fixture. Fix (cm-lifehacks wording, demo-builder applies): 'This one check is not a forecast of later recall, but it does show which step to fix.' | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): DISPUTED. It is no longer the general empirical negative disputed in passes 38-41. Support convention fits a stipulated exercise.

recall.question: You felt sure of a 4-step route. Written from memory, steps 1, 2 and 4 match your notes. What do you now know?
options: Step 3 is the one to fix
